monument_name: Kva Hiti (probably built during the Licchavi period)
description_en: During the Licchavi period (3rd-9th cent.), the city of Kathmandu was geographically divided into two sections: Dakṣiṇakoligrāma (Yaṃgala) and Koligrāma (Yambu). As the settlement stretched, the city was divided into three sections during the Malla period (13th-15th cent.). The northern section came to be known as Thaḥne, the upper region, while the central area of Maru was called Dathu. Likewise, the lower section of Kathmandu in the south was referred to as Kvaḥne. This geographical division still exists. A famous Newar folk song of the medieval period accounts the three water spouts of the three sections of Kathmandu: The Thã Hiti of Thaḥne, Kva Hiti of Kvaḥne and Maru Hiti at the centre. The Kva Hiti got its name from its geographical location at the lower part of the city in the south known as Kvaḥne.Of the two spouts, water flows from only the one at the centre (KAT0890-001) at present; the other smaller spout (KAT0890-004) has already run dry. There is a Licchavi Caitya, ajaḥdhuṃ, fourśivaliṅgas, and statues of Umāmaheśvara, Gaṇeśa and Sūrya in the Hiti premises.There are no historical sources to date the initial construction of the Hiti. However, the presence of above-mentioned Licchavi Caitya in the Hiti premises suggests that it must have been constructed sometime during that period. There is a mention of the Kva Hiti in a palm-leaf manuscript dated NS 736 (1616 CE) (cf.S.M. Rājavaṃśī2040, p. 42). The source of water of this Hiti was dug up and renovated in NS 902 (1782 CE). Acaityawas also established on the same occasion. The Hiti was renovated in around VS 2032 (1975 CE) as well. A Licchavi inscription was recovered while digging up the area then. Unfortunately, the inscription was lost.Every year during the Sithi Nakhaḥ festival (held on the 6th of the bright fortnight of Jyeṣṭha), locals clean the Hiti. The Lakṣmaṇa Āḥju Śrāddha Guthi performs the anniversary ritual of the mentioned Licchavi Caitya at the Hiti every year on the full moon day of Āśvina. They also distributesamaybajion this occasion.
description_ne: लिच्छविकालमा काठमाडौंलाई दक्षिणकोलिग्राम (यंगल) र कोलिग्राम (यम्बु) मा विभाजन गरिएको थियो । मल्लकालमा यस शहरमा धेरै टोलहरु भए र यो शहरलाई तीन भागमा बाँडियो । त्यसबेला माथिल्लो (उत्तरतिरको) भागलाई थःने, बीचको भाग (काष्ठमण्डप/मरु) लाई दथु र तल्लो (दक्षिणतिरको) भागलाई क्वःने भनी मुख्य रूपले विभाजन गरेको पाइन्छ । यो विभाजन परम्परा आजसम्म पनि नेवार समुदायमा चलि नै रहेको पाइन्छ । मल्लकालमा प्रचलित ‘राजमति’ शीर्षकको लोकगीतबाट पनि यो कुरा थाहा हुन्छ । उक्त गीतमा एक ठाउँमा थःनेया थँहिति, क्वःनेया क्वहिति, दथुइ लाक्क मरुहिति अर्थात् माथिको माथिल्लो धारा थँहिति, तलको तल्लो धारा क्वहिति र बीचको धारा मरुहिति भनिएको छ । काठमाडौंको दक्षिणतिरको क्वःने (तल्लो भेगमा) बनाइएको हिति हुनाले यस हितिको नाम क्व हिति रहन गएको हो । यस हितिमा पश्चिमाभिमुख गरी दुईवटा टुटी बनाइएक छन । ती दुईमध्ये बीचमा रहेको टुटी (KAT0890-001) बाट मात्र पानी झर्छ, सानो टुटी (KAT0890-004) बाट पानी झर्दैन । हितिमा एउटा लिच्छविकालीन चैत्य, जःरुँहिति सहित चारवटा शिवलिङ्ग र उमामहेश्वर, गणेश, सूर्यका मूर्तिहरू स्थापना गरिएका छन् ।यो हितिको स्थापनाबारे कुनै अभिलेख प्राप्त भएको छैन । हितिमा लिच्छवि चैत्य स्थापना गरिएको हुनाले लिच्छविकालमै हिति निर्माण गरिएको हुनसक्छ । नेसं ७३६ (सन् १६१६) को ताडपत्रमा क्व हितिको उल्लेख गरिएको छ (S.M. Rājavaṃśī2040, p. 42) । नेसं ९०२ (सन् १७८२) मा हितिमा खनेर मुहानको जीर्णोद्धार गर्नुका साथै चैत्य पनि मर्मत गरिएको थियो । विसं २०३२ (सन् १९७५) सालतिर पनि हितिको जीर्णोद्धार गरिएको थियो । त्यसबेला खन्ने क्रममा लिच्छविकालको शिलापत्र पनि भेटिएको थियो, पछि त्यो शिलापत्र हरायो ।प्रत्येक वर्ष ज्येष्ठ शुक्ल ६ सिथिनखःको दिनमा टोलवासीहरू मिलेर हिति सफा गरिन्छ । प्रत्येक वर्ष आश्विन शुक्ल पूर्णिमाको दिनमा लक्ष्मण आःजु श्राद्ध गुठीको तर्फबाट हितिमा रहेको लिच्छविकालीन चैत्यको वर्षबन्धन पूजा गरी समयबजि वितरण गरिन्छ ।

historical_events.event_description: The Hiti is mentioned in a palm-leaf manuscript from NS 736.

historical_events.event_name: Repair of the Hiti and Caitya
historical_events.event_description: Jayacakra Siṃha, Bhājudhana and other family members jointly repaired the Hiti and the Licchavi Caitya in memory of their deceased family members.

In around 1975 CE, the Hiti had turned into a pond because its drainage system did not work properly. Locals tried to repair the drainage system but were unsuccessful. The pond drained out due course of time, but the Hiti dried up. Thus, locals started digging up the water channel to reach the source of the Hiti. Before they reached the source, the Hiti started to flow again.
